claim: DET1 is an evolutionarily conserved component of the ubiquitination machinery that mediates the destabilization of key regulators of cell differentiation and proliferation in multicellular organisms.
source: DE-ETIOLATED 1 (DET1) is an evolutionarily conserved component of the ubiquitination machinery that mediates the destabilization of key regulators of cell differentiation and proliferation in multicellular organisms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: DET1 is essential for the regulation of histone H2B monoubiquitination (H2Bub) over most genes by controlling the stability of a deubiquitination module (DUBm).
source: In this study, we provide evidence from Arabidopsis that DET1 is essential for the regulation of histone H2B monoubiquitination (H2Bub) over most genes by controlling the stability of a deubiquitination module (DUBm).
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The Arabidopsis DUBm only comprises three proteins (SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22).
source: In contrast with yeast and metazoan DUB modules that are associated with the large SAGA complex, the Arabidopsis DUBm only comprises three proteins (hereafter named SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22) and appears to act independently as a major H2Bub deubiquitinase activity.
evidence: This is supported by TAP purification data shown in Figure 4A and reciprocal analyses.

claim: The Arabidopsis DUBm appears to act independently as a major H2Bub deubiquitinase activity.
source: In contrast with yeast and metazoan DUB modules that are associated with the large SAGA complex, the Arabidopsis DUBm only comprises three proteins (hereafter named SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22) and appears to act independently as a major H2Bub deubiquitinase activity.
evidence: This is supported by the absence of SGF73 ortholog and size-exclusion chromatography data in Figure 4E.

claim: DET1-DDB1-Associated-1 (DDA1) protein interacts with SGF11 in vivo.
source: Our study further unveils that DET1-DDB1-Associated-1 (DDA1) protein interacts with SGF11 in vivo, linking the DET1 complex to light-dependent ubiquitin-mediated proteolytic degradation of the DUBm.
evidence: This is supported by Y2H, BiFC, and pull-down assays shown in Figure 3.

claim: DDA1 interaction with SGF11 links the DET1 complex to light-dependent ubiquitin-mediated proteolytic degradation of the DUBm.
source: Our study further unveils that DET1-DDB1-Associated-1 (DDA1) protein interacts with SGF11 in vivo, linking the DET1 complex to light-dependent ubiquitin-mediated proteolytic degradation of the DUBm.
evidence: This is supported by data showing light-dependent degradation of SGF11 in a DET1-dependent manner (Figure 6).

claim: DET1 null mutations are lethal in plants.
source: DET1 null mutations are lethal in plants (Miséra et al., 1994; Pepper et al., 1994), Drosophila (Berloco et al., 2001) and Human (Wertz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DET1 null mutations are lethal in Drosophila.
source: DET1 null mutations are lethal in plants (Miséra et al., 1994; Pepper et al., 1994), Drosophila (Berloco et al., 2001) and Human (Wertz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Berloco et al., 2001.

claim: DET1 null mutations are lethal in Human.
source: DET1 null mutations are lethal in plants (Miséra et al., 1994; Pepper et al., 1994), Drosophila (Berloco et al., 2001) and Human (Wertz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wertz et al., 2004.

claim: DET1 is a central integrator of light signaling in plants.
source: However, viable Arabidopsis knockdown alleles identified in genetic screens for mutant plants displaying a constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype (i.e. de-etiolated) have unveiled that DET1 is a central integrator of light signaling in plants (Chory et al., 1989; Pepper et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to genetic studies.

claim: The Arabidopsis det1-1 mutation affects the expression of thousands of nuclear genes.
source: The Arabidopsis det1-1 mutation affects the expression of thousands of nuclear genes (Ma et al., 2003; Schroeder et al., 2002), partly because proteolytic degradation of the proto-photomorphogenic transcription factor HY5 is abolished in this background, thereby mimicking the presence of light on the transcriptional program (Osterlund et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous transcriptomic studies.

claim: Proteolytic degradation of the proto-photomorphogenic transcription factor HY5 is abolished in det1-1 background.
source: The Arabidopsis det1-1 mutation affects the expression of thousands of nuclear genes (Ma et al., 2003; Schroeder et al., 2002), partly because proteolytic degradation of the proto-photomorphogenic transcription factor HY5 is abolished in this background, thereby mimicking the presence of light on the transcriptional program (Osterlund et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Osterlund et al., 2000.

claim: In humans, DET1 controls the stability of cell proliferation factors such as the Cdt1 DNA replication-licensing factor.
source: In humans, DET1 also controls the stability of cell proliferation factors such as the Cdt1 DNA replication-licensing factor (Pick et al., 2007) and the proto-oncogenic transcription factor c-Jun (Wertz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pick et al., 2007.

claim: In humans, DET1 controls the stability of the proto-oncogenic transcription factor c-Jun.
source: In humans, DET1 also controls the stability of cell proliferation factors such as the Cdt1 DNA replication-licensing factor (Pick et al., 2007) and the proto-oncogenic transcription factor c-Jun (Wertz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wertz et al., 2004.

claim: DET1 is an atypical DAMAGED DNA BINDING PROTEIN 1 (DDB1)-CULLIN4 (CUL4) Associated Factor (DCAF) acting with the small DDA1 protein to provide specificity to one or more E3 CUL4-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRL4).
source: Accordingly, a currently accepted model in both plants and animals is that DET1 is an atypical DAMAGED DNA BINDING PROTEIN 1 (DDB1)-CULLIN4 (CUL4) Associated Factor (DCAF) acting with the small DDA1 (DET1-DDB1-Associated 1) protein to provide specificity to one or more E3 CUL4-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRL4) (Chory, 2010; Lau and Deng, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: DET1, DDA1, DDB1 and COP10 proteins constitute a substrate adaptor module (C3D) within CRL4 complexes.
source: For this activity, DET1 and DDA1, together with DDB1 and CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENIC 10 (COP10) proteins, constitute a substrate adaptor module (COP10-DET1-DDB1-DDA1; hereafter termed C3D) within CRL4 complexes (Irigoyen et al., 2014; Pick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: C3D binding to the CUL4 scaffolding protein is mediated by the core adaptor subunit DDB1.
source: C3D binding to the CUL4 scaffolding protein is mediated by the core adaptor subunit DDB1 whereas the E2 ubiquitin conjugase variant COP10 likely acts to increase the activity of CRL4 complexes towards specific protein targets (Lau and Deng, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: The E2 ubiquitin conjugase variant COP10 likely acts to increase the activity of CRL4 complexes towards specific protein targets.
source: C3D binding to the CUL4 scaffolding protein is mediated by the core adaptor subunit DDB1 whereas the E2 ubiquitin conjugase variant COP10 likely acts to increase the activity of CRL4 complexes towards specific protein targets (Lau and Deng, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article and uses the word 'likely' indicating some uncertainty.

claim: Photomorphogenesis is a developmental switch that initiates upon the first perception of light by young plants reaching the soil surface.
source: Photomorphogenesis is a developmental switch that initiates upon the first perception of light by young plants reaching the soil surface.
evidence: This is a well-established concept in plant biology supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Photomorphogenesis triggers the launching of organ growth and the establishment of photosynthesis through the differentiation of primary leaf (cotyledon) cells.
source: This transition triggers the launching of organ growth and the establishment of photosynthesis, most notably through the differentiation of primary leaf (cotyledon) cells (reviewed in [Casal, 2013; Seluzicki et al., 2017; Wu, 2014]).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Photomorphogenesis involves changes at transcriptomic, epigenomic and nuclear architecture levels.
source: The process involves changes at transcriptomic, epigenomic and nuclear architecture levels (Bourbousse et al., 2015; Charron et al., 2009; Sullivan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DET1 has high affinity for nucleosomal histone H2B in vitro and in vivo.
source: While several chromatin modifiers are known to influence light-responsive gene expression, the first direct link between light signaling and chromatin came from the discovery that DET1 has high affinity for nucleosomal histone H2B in vitro and in vivo (Benvenuto et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Benvenuto et al., 2002.

claim: Histone H2B monoubiquitination acts cooperatively with RNA Polymerase II and other PTMs of histones to promote gene expression and the regulation of cellular homeostasis in various organisms.
source: This histone post-translational modification (PTM) acts cooperatively with RNA Polymerase II (RNA Pol II) and other PTMs of histones to promote gene expression and the regulation of cellular homeostasis in various organisms (Shema et al., 2008; Smith and Shilatifard, 2013; Weake and Workman, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, the PAF1 complex interacts with Ser-5 phosphorylated RNA Pol II and serves as a platform for H2B monoubiquitination by the Rad6 E2 ubiquitin conjugase and the Bre1 E3 ligase.
source: In the sequence of events established in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the Polymerase-associated factor 1 (PAF1) complex interacts with Ser-5 phosphorylated RNA Pol II and serves as a platform for H2B monoubiquitination by the Rad6 E2 ubiquitin conjugase and the Bre1 E3 ligase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the yeast system.

claim: Recruitment of the SAGA complex at the Pre-Initiation Complex triggers H2Bub de-ubiquitination and phosphorylation of Pol II CTD on Ser-2, mediating the transition towards transcription elongation.
source: In turn, recruitment of the SAGA (Spt-Ada-Gcn5-acetyltransferase) complex at the Pre-Initiation Complex (PIC) triggers H2Bub de-ubiquitination and phosphorylation of Pol II CTD on Ser-2, mediating the transition towards transcription elongation (Wyce et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wyce et al., 2007.

claim: SAGA is thought to travel along the gene body with RNA Pol II to allow for repeated cycles of histone H2B ubiquitination/de-ubiquitination by opposing Bre1 activity.
source: Sliding from the promoter, SAGA is thought to travel along the gene body with RNA Pol II to allow for repeated cycles of histone H2B ubiquitination/de-ubiquitination by opposing Bre1 activity (Henry et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a model supported by citation, indicated by 'is thought to'.

claim: H2B ubiquitination/de-ubiquitination cycles facilitate the progression of RNA Pol II through nucleosomal barriers by influencing DNA accessibility, recruitment of the histone chaperone FACT and promoting nucleosome reassembly.
source: This is thought to facilitate the progression of RNA Pol II through nucleosomal barriers by influencing DNA accessibility, recruitment of the histone chaperone FACT (FAcilitates Chromatin Transcription) and promoting nucleosome reassembly (Belotserkovskaya et al., 2003; Fierz et al., 2011; Fleming et al., 2008; Pavri et al., 2006; Xin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: SAGA displays a general co-activator activity that promotes transcription at a post-initiation step on most expressed genes in budding yeast.
source: Accordingly, SAGA displays a general co-activator activity that promotes transcription at a post-initiation step on most expressed genes in budding yeast (Baptista et al., 2017; Bonnet et al., 2014), with a pronounced effect on so-called SAGA-bound 'regulatable' genes (de Jonge et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: In budding yeast and metazoans, SAGA is a ~ 1.8 megaDa gigantic complex made of functionally distinct components comprising a TAF architectural core module, a TBP module, a HAT module, and a H2Bub deubiquitination module (DUBm).
source: In budding yeast and metazoans, SAGA is a ~ 1.8 megaDa gigantic complex made of functionally distinct components comprising a TBP-associated factor (TAF) architectural core module, a TATA-Binding Protein (TBP) module, a histone acetyltransferase (HAT) module, and a H2Bub deubiquitination module (DUBm) (Grant et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Grant et al., 1997.

claim: DUBm is an independent structure that functionally requires the Ubp8 catalytic subunit, the Sgf11 nucleosome-binding subunit and the small protein Sus1, which binds ubiquitin.
source: DUBm is an independent structure that functionally requires the Ubiquitin protease 8 (Ubp8) catalytic subunit, the Sgf11 (SAGA-associated factor 11) nucleosome-binding subunit and the small protein Sus1 (Sl gene upstream of ySa1), which binds ubiquitin (Rodríguez-Navarro, 2009), while the fourth subunit Sgf73 makes the bridge with core SAGA modules (Köhler et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The fourth DUBm subunit Sgf73 makes the bridge with core SAGA modules.
source: DUBm is an independent structure that functionally requires the Ubiquitin protease 8 (Ubp8) catalytic subunit, the Sgf11 (SAGA-associated factor 11) nucleosome-binding subunit and the small protein Sus1 (Sl gene upstream of ySa1), which binds ubiquitin (Rodríguez-Navarro, 2009), while the fourth subunit Sgf73 makes the bridge with core SAGA modules (Köhler et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Köhler et al., 2008 and Lee et al., 2009.

claim: Orthologous proteins of Ubp8, Sgf11 and Sus1 or their human counterparts USP22, ATXN7L3 and ENY2 have been identified from the genome sequence of Arabidopsis thaliana.
source: Orthologous proteins of Ubp8, Sgf11 and Sus1 or their human counterparts USP22, ATXN7L3 and ENY2 have been identified from the genome sequence of Arabidopsis thaliana but Sgf73 appears to be absent (Moraga and Aquea, 2015; Srivastava et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Moraga and Aquea, 2015 and Srivastava et al., 2015.

claim: Sgf73 appears to be absent from the Arabidopsis genome.
source: Orthologous proteins of Ubp8, Sgf11 and Sus1 or their human counterparts USP22, ATXN7L3 and ENY2 have been identified from the genome sequence of Arabidopsis thaliana but Sgf73 appears to be absent (Moraga and Aquea, 2015; Srivastava et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations and the authors' own bioinformatic searches.

claim: Arabidopsis UBIQUITIN PROTEASE 26 (UBP26) deubiquitinates H2Bub in vivo, impacting expression of the FLC developmental regulator.
source: Arabidopsis UBIQUITIN PROTEASE 26 (UBP26) deubiquitinates H2Bub in vivo, impacting expression of the FLC developmental regulator (Schmitz et al., 2009), but it appears to act independently from SAGA and rather displays a repressive activity on transposable elements (Sridhar et al., 2007) and imprinted genes (Luo et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: UBP26 appears to act independently from SAGA and rather displays a repressive activity on transposable elements and imprinted genes.
source: Arabidopsis UBIQUITIN PROTEASE 26 (UBP26) deubiquitinates H2Bub in vivo, impacting expression of the FLC developmental regulator (Schmitz et al., 2009), but it appears to act independently from SAGA and rather displays a repressive activity on transposable elements (Sridhar et al., 2007) and imprinted genes (Luo et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sridhar et al., 2007 and Luo et al., 2008.

claim: Recent purification of elongating RNA Pol II has shown its tight association with chromatin machineries such as PAF1, FACT and HUB complex subunits in Arabidopsis.
source: Recent purification of elongating RNA Pol II has indeed shown its tight association with chromatin machineries such as PAF1, FACT and HUB complex subunits in Arabidopsis (Antosz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Antosz et al., 2017.

claim: HUB is the only known histone H2B E3 ubiquitin ligase in Arabidopsis, acting as a heterotetramer of the HUB1 and HUB2 proteins.
source: HUB is the only known histone H2B E3 ubiquitin ligase in Arabidopsis, acting as a heterotetramer of the HISTONE UBIQUITINATION 1 (HUB1) and HUB2 proteins (reviewed in Feng and Shen, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Null mutations in HUB1 or HUB2 genes abolish H2Bub deposition.
source: Although null mutations in HUB1 or HUB2 genes abolish H2Bub deposition, knockout plants are viable with only mild phenotypic defects in seed dormancy, cell cycle progression, circadian clock and flowering time control (Cao et al., 2008; Fleury et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: HUB1 or HUB2 knockout plants are viable with only mild phenotypic defects in seed dormancy, cell cycle progression, circadian clock and flowering time control.
source: Although null mutations in HUB1 or HUB2 genes abolish H2Bub deposition, knockout plants are viable with only mild phenotypic defects in seed dormancy, cell cycle progression, circadian clock and flowering time control (Cao et al., 2008; Fleury et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cao et al., 2008; Fleury et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2007.

claim: Abrogating HUB1 function impairs rapid modulation of RNA levels of light-regulated genes during seedling photomorphogenesis.
source: Still, abrogating HUB1 function impairs rapid modulation of RNA levels of light-regulated genes during seedling photomorphogenesis, suggesting that monoubiquitinated H2B is required to attain high expression levels during Arabidopsis photomorphogenesis (Bourbousse et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bourbousse et al., 2012.

claim: Monoubiquitinated H2B is required to attain high expression levels during Arabidopsis photomorphogenesis.
source: Still, abrogating HUB1 function impairs rapid modulation of RNA levels of light-regulated genes during seedling photomorphogenesis, suggesting that monoubiquitinated H2B is required to attain high expression levels during Arabidopsis photomorphogenesis (Bourbousse et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citation to Bourbousse et al., 2012.

claim: Label-free quantitative mass spectrometry analysis identified 15 different peptide sequences bearing one or more differentially modified residues in det1-1 seedlings, half of them matching histone H2B.
source: We identified 15 different peptide sequences bearing one or more differentially modified residues in det1-1 seedlings, half of them matching histone H2B (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Histone H2B was found to be more frequently acetylated and twice less monoubiquitinated at a conserved lysine residue in the carboxy-terminal tail of 9 different H2B isoforms in det1-1 mutants.
source: Histone H2B was found to be more frequently acetylated and twice less monoubiquitinated at a conserved lysine residue in the carboxy-terminal tail of 9 different H2B isoforms (Figure 1A–B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Low H2Bub levels in det1-1 mutant plants were reproducibly visualized by immunoblot detection.
source: Low H2Bub levels in these mutant plants were reproducibly visualized by immunoblot detection using an antibody that recognizes H2B histone isoforms and their slower migrating monoubiquitinated forms in chromatin-enriched samples (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Remaining H2Bub marks in det1-1 plants are deposited via the HUB pathway.
source: Finally, introgression of the hub1-3 mutation in the det1-1 genetic background indicated that remaining H2Bub marks in det1-1 plants are deposited via the HUB pathway (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by genetic data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The mass spectrometry analysis indicated an increase of histone H3 methylation on Lys-27 or Lys-36 in det1-1 mutants.
source: The mass spectrometry analysis also indicated an increase of histone H3 methylation on Lys-27 or Lys-36, but no robust differences in H3K36me3 or H3K27me3 could be detected by immunoblot analysis (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data, though immunoblot did not confirm it.

claim: No robust differences in H3K36me3 or H3K27me3 could be detected by immunoblot analysis in det1-1 mutants.
source: The mass spectrometry analysis also indicated an increase of histone H3 methylation on Lys-27 or Lys-36, but no robust differences in H3K36me3 or H3K27me3 could be detected by immunoblot analysis (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Immunoblot analyses detected increased H3K9ac levels and reduction of H3K27ac levels in det1-1 mutants.
source: Instead, complementary immunoblot analyses of euchromatic histone marks detected increased H3K9ac levels and reduction of H3K27ac levels in det1-1 (Figure 1C), which had not been found by mass spectrometry.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: H2Bub domains were largely restricted to the transcribed regions.
source: Consistent with our previous findings obtained by ChIP-chip (Bourbousse et al., 2012; Roudier et al., 2011), H2Bub domains were largely restricted to the transcribed regions.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data and citations to previous studies.

claim: A set of ~6900 genes consistently bear a H2Bub peak in all four samples (WT light, WT dark, det1-1 light, det1-1 dark).
source: While a set of ~6900 genes consistently bear a H2Bub peak in all four samples, the number of marked genes in det1-1 compared to WT plants was 19% lower in the light (2134 fewer genes) and 26% lower in the dark (2577 fewer genes) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The number of H2Bub-marked genes in det1-1 compared to WT plants was 19% lower in the light (2134 fewer genes).
source: While a set of ~6900 genes consistently bear a H2Bub peak in all four samples, the number of marked genes in det1-1 compared to WT plants was 19% lower in the light (2134 fewer genes) and 26% lower in the dark (2577 fewer genes) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The number of H2Bub-marked genes in det1-1 compared to WT plants was 26% lower in the dark (2577 fewer genes).
source: While a set of ~6900 genes consistently bear a H2Bub peak in all four samples, the number of marked genes in det1-1 compared to WT plants was 19% lower in the light (2134 fewer genes) and 26% lower in the dark (2577 fewer genes) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Quantification using Rx scaling factors unveiled a severe decrease of H2Bub average level over the set of marked genes in det1-1 seedlings, which was similarly observed in both light conditions.
source: Quantification using Rx scaling factors unveiled a severe decrease of H2Bub average level over the set of marked genes in det1-1 seedlings, which was similarly observed in both light conditions (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: H2Bub is decreased over almost all genes in det1-1 plants, regardless of the light condition.
source: Identification of the H2Bub-marked genes that are differentially ubiquitinated (DUGs) further showed that H2Bub is decreased over almost all genes in det1-1 plants, regardless of the light condition (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: det1-1 mutation has a broad effect on gene expression and largely mimics the effect of light on the transcriptome of dark-grown seedlings.
source: As previously reported (Schroeder et al., 2002), RNA-seq analyses performed on the same samples showed that det1-1 mutation has a broad effect on gene expression, to a large extent mimicking the effect of light signals on the transcriptome in dark conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and citation to Schroeder et al., 2002.

claim: In both dark and light conditions, gene expression misregulation occurred in a globally hypo-ubiquitinated H2B landscape in det1-1 plants.
source: In both dark and light conditions, gene expression misregulation occurred in a globally hypo-ubiquitinated H2B landscape in det1-1 plants (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by combined ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Small variations in H2Bub levels between dark and light-grown samples correlating with transcript levels could be detected in det1-1 plants, although to a much lower extent than in wild-type plants.
source: Small variations in H2Bub levels between dark and light-grown samples correlating with transcript levels could be detected in det1-1 plants, although to a much lower extent than in wild-type plants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DET1 impacts the whole H2Bub landscape, without apparent gene specificity and without clear functional impact on steady state transcript profiles.
source: All together, these observations indicate that DET1 impacts the whole H2Bub landscape, without apparent gene specificity and without clear functional impact on steady state transcript profiles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data presented.

claim: Variations in H2Bub levels correlating with transcript levels between dark and light conditions could be detected over hundreds of genes in WT plants.
source: In line with the role of H2Bub in the induction of light-responsive genes (Bourbousse et al., 2012), variations in H2Bub levels correlating with transcript levels between dark and light conditions could be detected over hundreds of genes in WT plants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and citation to Bourbousse et al., 2012.

claim: The upregulated HCF173 gene involved in the Photosystem II biogenesis under light conditions was detected as being hyper-ubiquitinated.
source: For example, the upregulated HCF173 gene involved in the Photosystem II biogenesis under light conditions (Schult et al., 2007) was detected as being hyper-ubiquitinated (hyper-Differentially Ubiquitinated Gene or hyper-DUG) (Figure 2—source data 1) and visually displayed higher H2Bub levels in WT (L) than in WT (D) samples (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2F and citation to Schult et al., 2007.

claim: The light-repressed HCAR gene involved in chlorophyll breakdown in darkness was detected as a hypo-DUG.
source: Vice versa, the light-repressed HCAR gene involved in chlorophyll breakdown in darkness (Sakuraba et al., 2013) was detected as a hypo-DUG, and visually displays reduced H2Bub levels over its coding sequence (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2F and citation to Sakuraba et al., 2013.

claim: Comparison of light- and dark-grown WT plants unveiled a global tendency in higher H2Bub chromatin enrichment in the light than in the dark condition.
source: More unexpectedly, comparison of light- and dark-grown WT plants further unveiled a global tendency in higher H2Bub chromatin enrichment in the light than in the dark condition.
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of ChIP-seq evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: The number of H2Bub-marked genes was 12% higher in light compared to dark condition in WT plants.
source: As compared to the dark condition, in the light i) the number of H2Bub-marked genes was 12% higher (Figure 2A), ii) H2Bub average enrichment was higher in meta-plots representing all 11,921 H2Bub-marked genes (Figure 2C) and accordingly, iii) hyper-DUGs in the light were 10 times more numerous than hypo-DUGs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: H2Bub average enrichment was higher in light than dark in meta-plots representing all 11,921 H2Bub-marked genes in WT plants.
source: As compared to the dark condition, in the light i) the number of H2Bub-marked genes was 12% higher (Figure 2A), ii) H2Bub average enrichment was higher in meta-plots representing all 11,921 H2Bub-marked genes (Figure 2C) and accordingly, iii) hyper-DUGs in the light were 10 times more numerous than hypo-DUGs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Hyper-DUGs in the light were 10 times more numerous than hypo-DUGs in WT plants.
source: As compared to the dark condition, in the light i) the number of H2Bub-marked genes was 12% higher (Figure 2A), ii) H2Bub average enrichment was higher in meta-plots representing all 11,921 H2Bub-marked genes (Figure 2C) and accordingly, iii) hyper-DUGs in the light were 10 times more numerous than hypo-DUGs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: An equivalent number of genes are up- and down-regulated by light in WT seedlings.
source: Comparison of relative transcript levels in dark- and light-grown WT seedlings showed that an equivalent number of genes are up- and down-regulated by light (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), with similar amplitude in transcript level variations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and 1D.

claim: Relative changes in gene expression do not seem to explain the global tendency for higher H2Bub enrichment in the light versus dark condition.
source: Consequently, on their own, relative changes in gene expression do not seem to explain the global tendency for higher H2Bub enrichment in the light versus dark condition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: H2Bub is globally more abundant on genes in photomorphogenic than in etiolated seedlings, a light-driven dynamic that is lost upon DET1 loss-of-function.
source: These findings unveil that H2Bub is globally more abundant on genes in photomophogenic than in etiolated seedlings, a light-driven dynamic that is lost upon DET1 loss-of-function.
evidence: This is a summary of the ChIP-seq findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: A Y2H screen using DDA1 as bait reproducibly detected the coding sequence of AT5G58575, a gene recently identified as the closest Arabidopsis ortholog of yeast Sgf11.
source: However, a Y2H screen using DDA1 as bait reproducibly detected the coding sequence of AT5G58575, a gene recently identified as the closest Arabidopsis ortholog of yeast Sgf11 (Moraga and Aquea, 2015; Srivastava et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by Y2H data and citations to Moraga and Aquea, 2015 and Srivastava et al., 2015.

claim: AT5G58575 (SGF11) encodes a protein with 31% and 19% sequence similarity with the SAGA DUB module component Sgf11/ATXN7L3 from S. cerevisiae and human, respectively.
source: AT5G58575, hereafter referred to as SGF11, encodes a protein with 31% and 19% sequence similarity with the SAGA DUB module component Sgf11/ATXN7L3 from S. cerevisiae and human, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Reciprocal Y2H assays using a 3AT chase control confirmed the specific association of DDA1 with SGF11.
source: Reciprocal Y2H assays using a 3AT chase control confirmed the specific association of DDA1 with SGF11 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: BiFC assays in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves showed that SGF11 associates with DDA1 in plant nuclei.
source: Bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves further showed that SGF11 associates with DDA1 in plant nuclei (Figure 3B) but neither with DET1 nor with the other two C3D components COP10 and DDB1a (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: SGF11 does not associate with DET1, COP10, or DDB1a in BiFC assays.
source: Bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves further showed that SGF11 associates with DDA1 in plant nuclei (Figure 3B) but neither with DET1 nor with the other two C3D components COP10 and DDB1a (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: DDA1 and SGF11 were found to associate in Arabidopsis extracts using semi-in vivo MBP fusion pull-down assays.
source: Finally, DDA1 and SGF11 were found to associate in Arabidopsis extracts using semi-in vivo maltose-binding protein (MBP) fusion pull-down assays (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: DET1 and SGF11 are associated, although with a lower efficiency than DDA1 and SGF11.
source: Similar MBP assays showed that DET1 and SGF11 are also associated, although with a lower efficiency (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: DDA1 physically associates with SGF11, a link that potentially allows bridging the C3D complex to a SAGA-like H2Bub deubiquitination activity.
source: We conclude from these analyses that DDA1 physically associates with SGF11, a link that potentially allows bridging the C3D complex to a SAGA-like H2Bub deubiquitination activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the protein interaction data presented.

claim: TAP analysis of SGF11 consistently identified peptides from four proteins in addition to SGF11 itself: two cytosolic TONNEAU1A/B proteins as well as AT3G27100 and AT5G10790.
source: Given the lack of knowledge on SAGA DUBm composition, structure and activity in the plant kingdom, we carried out Tandem Affinity Purification (TAP) analysis of SGF11 constitutively expressed in Arabidopsis cell cultures grown under either light or dark conditions (Figure 4A). This consistently identified peptides from four proteins in addition to SGF11 itself: two cytosolic TONNEAU1A/B proteins (Traas et al., 1987) as well as AT3G27100 and AT5G10790, two orthologous proteins of the yeast/Drosophila and human DUBm subunits SUS1/ENY2 and UBP22/USP22 proteins, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by TAP-MS data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: AT3G27100 and AT5G10790 are orthologous proteins of the yeast/Drosophila and human DUBm subunits SUS1/ENY2 and UBP22/USP22 proteins, respectively.
source: This consistently identified peptides from four proteins in addition to SGF11 itself: two cytosolic TONNEAU1A/B proteins (Traas et al., 1987) as well as AT3G27100 and AT5G10790, two orthologous proteins of the yeast/Drosophila and human DUBm subunits SUS1/ENY2 and UBP22/USP22 proteins, respectively.
evidence: This is based on sequence homology analysis.

claim: Reciprocal TAP analyses using UBP22 as bait identified only SGF11 and ENY2.
source: Reciprocal TAP analyses using UBP22 as bait identified only SGF11 and ENY2 (Figure 4—source data 1), thus confirming robust and specific co-purification of these three proteins.
evidence: This is supported by TAP-MS data shown in Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: TAP analyses allowed the co-purification of three of the four known SAGA DUBm subunits, SGF73 being conspicuously absent.
source: Altogether, our TAP analyses allowed the co-purification of three of the four known SAGA DUBm subunits, SGF73 being conspicuously absent.
evidence: This is a summary of the TAP-MS results.

claim: The Arabidopsis genome apparently encodes no orthologous proteins of the yeast/human SGF73/ATXN7.
source: Noteworthy, the Arabidopsis genome apparently encodes no orthologous proteins of the yeast/human SGF73/ATXN7 (Moraga and Aquea, 2015; Srivastava et al., 2015), a subunit that is required for stabilizing and bridging DUBm to SAGA in other species (Durand et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations and the authors' own bioinformatic searches.

claim: SGF73/ATXN7 is a subunit that is required for stabilizing and bridging DUBm to SAGA in other species.
source: Noteworthy, the Arabidopsis genome apparently encodes no orthologous proteins of the yeast/human SGF73/ATXN7 (Moraga and Aquea, 2015; Srivastava et al., 2015), a subunit that is required for stabilizing and bridging DUBm to SAGA in other species (Durand et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Durand et al., 2014.

claim: Y2H and BiFC experiments showed robust interactions of SGF11 with ENY2 and UBP22, but not between ENY2 and UBP22.
source: Y2H and BiFC experiments were conducted to assess the mode of association between SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22. As observed in S. cerevisiae (Köhler et al., 2006), both analyses showed robust interactions of SGF11 with ENY2 and UBP22, but not between ENY2 and UBP22 (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is supported by Y2H and BiFC data shown in Figure 4B-C and citation to Köhler et al., 2006.

claim: The modeled structure of the Arabidopsis DUBm displayed high similarity to the yeast DUBm X-ray structure made of the four Sgf11, Ubp8, Sus1 and Sgf73 proteins.
source: To access how SGF11 might bridge ENY2 to UBP22 in the absence of an SGF73/ATXN7 ortholog, we modeled the tri-dimensional structure of the Arabidopsis DUBm based on their sequence homology with proteins of known structure. The best confidence model displayed high similarity to the yeast DUBm X-ray structure made of the four Sgf11, Ubp8, Sus1 and Sgf73 proteins (Samara et al., 2010) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by structural modeling shown in Figure 4D and citation to Samara et al., 2010.

claim: The modeled structure shows conservation of the UBP22 Zn-finger domains positioning, in particular that potentially forming the conserved assembly lobe.
source: This representation shows conservation of the UBP22 Zn-finger domains positioning, in particular that potentially forming the conserved assembly lobe by encapsulating the long SGF11 amino-terminal α-helix with the central part of the small ENY2 protein (Köhler et al., 2010; Samara et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling and citations to Köhler et al., 2010 and Samara et al., 2010.

claim: The small ENY2 protein forms an interface between the UBP22 C-terminal domain and the long SGF11 α-helix, which may re-enforce the pairwise protein interactions in the DUBm.
source: The small ENY2 protein forms an interface between the UBP22 C-terminal domain and the long SGF11 α-helix, which may re-enforce the pairwise protein interactions in the DUBm (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SGF11 C-terminal zinc-finger potentially allows interaction with a nucleosome and the ubiquitin moiety of H2Bub.
source: SGF11 C-terminal zinc-finger potentially allows interaction with a nucleosome and the ubiquitin moiety of H2Bub as shown in other species (Durand et al., 2014; Samara et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling and citations to studies in other species.

claim: Long plant-specific amino- and carboxy-terminal extensions may protrude out from the conserved structural domains, possibly linking this core structure to other proteins or replacing the SAGA bridging-function of Sgf73.
source: Interestingly, long plant-specific amino- and carboxy-terminal extensions may protrude out from the conserved structural domains, possibly linking this core structure to other proteins or replacing the SAGA bridging-function of Sgf73.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural modeling.

claim: All SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22 proteins are nuclear-localized.
source: Arabidopsis transgenic lines stably expressing GFP-tagged SGF11, ENY2 or UBP22 were generated and used to investigate their subcellular localization, confirming that all proteins are nuclear-localized (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: SGF11 and UBP22 displayed punctuated signals in the euchromatin and are visibly excluded from densely DAPI-stained heterochromatic chromocenters and from the nucleolus.
source: In agreement with the conserved function of SAGA in RNA Pol II transcription regulation, confocal imaging after anti-GFP immunolabeling further showed that SGF11 and UBP22 displayed punctuated signals in the euchromatin and are visibly excluded from densely DAPI-stained heterochromatic chromocenters and from the nucleolus.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: DDA1-GFP and MYC-DET1 proteins display euchromatic localization.
source: Euchromatic localization was also observed for DDA1-GFP and MYC-DET1 proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: GFP-ENY2 signals were reproducibly enriched both in the euchromatic and heterochromatic compartments, sometimes overlapping with nucleolus-associated chromocenters.
source: By contrast, GFP-ENY2 signals were reproducibly enriched both in the euchromatic and heterochromatic compartments, sometimes overlapping with nucleolus-associated chromocenters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Arabidopsis ENY2 might display another activity independently from SGF11 and UBP22 in Arabidopsis.
source: Though, at this stage we also cannot exclude that GFP-ENY2 signal in heterochromatic domains might artifactually result from its overexpression, Arabidopsis ENY2 might therefore display another activity independently from SGF11 and UBP22 in Arabidopsis.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the localization data.

claim: Arabidopsis SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22 associate in planta and potentially form a trimeric DUB module in the absence of an Sgf73/ATXN7 ortholog.
source: Taken together, these observations unveil that Arabidopsis SGF11, ENY2 and UBP22 associate in planta and potentially form a trimeric DUB module in the absence of an Sgf73/ATXN7 ortholog.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the TAP, Y2H, BiFC, and structural modeling data.

claim: Size-exclusion chromatography analysis showed that the ~100 kDa GFP-UBP22 protein was largely part of a 100–150 kDa complex, a size compatible with a tripartite association with the 20 kDa SGF11 and 13 kDa ENY2 proteins.
source: To assess the stable accumulation of such a complex, a size-exclusion chromatography analysis of soluble protein fractions from the UBP22::UBP22-GFP plant line was performed. The ~100 kDa GFP-UBP22 protein was largely part of a 100–150 kDa complex, a size compatible with a tripartite association with the 20 kDa SGF11 and 13 kDa ENY2 proteins (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: UBP22-GFP could also be detected (albeit to a much lower extent) in higher molecular weight fractions, which could correspond to SAGA-like complex size.
source: UBP22-GFP could also be detected (albeit to a much lower extent) in higher molecular weight fractions, which could correspond to SAGA-like complex size.
evidence: This is based on size-exclusion chromatography data and is speculative.

claim: Expression of the full-length UBP22 coding sequence under the control of the yeast CYC1 promoter successfully restored normal H2Bub levels in S. cerevisiae Ubp8 knockout strain.
source: To determine whether UBP22 displays H2Bub deubiquitination activity, we conducted a complementation assay of an S. cerevisiae Ubp8 knockout strain, a loss-of-function that induces aberrantly high H2Bub levels (Gardner et al., 2005; Henry et al., 2003). Expression of the full-length UBP22 coding sequence under the control of the yeast CYC1 promoter successfully restored normal H2Bub levels in independently transformed colonies (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by yeast complementation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: UBP22 can replace Ubp8 activity for H2Bub hydrolysis in the context of a bona fide SAGA complex.
source: UBP22 can therefore replace Ubp8 activity for H2Bub hydrolysis in the context of a bona fide SAGA complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the yeast complementation data.

claim: Homozygous ubp22-1, sgf11-1 and sgf11-2 plant lines were viable and displayed no obvious developmental phenotypes under standard laboratory growth conditions.
source: To further test the influence of the Arabidopsis DUBm on H2Bub in plants, we obtained T-DNA insertion lines for UBP22 and SGF11, hereafter referred to as ubp22-1, sgf11-1 and sgf11-2. All homozygous plant lines were viable and displayed no obvious developmental phenotypes under standard laboratory growth conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by phenotypic observation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Immunoblot analyses showed a robust increase of H2Bub levels in ubp22-1, sgf11-1 and sgf11-2 loss-of-function lines as compared to their wild-type counterparts, resulting in 2–3 fold more monoubiquitination of the histone H2B pool than in wild-type plants.
source: Immunoblot analyses showed a robust increase of H2Bub levels in each of these loss-of-function lines as compared to their wild-type counterparts, resulting in 2–3 fold more monoubiquitination of the histone H2B pool than in wild-type plants (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Re-introduction of a UBP22 or SGF11 functional coding sequence successfully restored low H2Bub levels in ubp22-1 and sgf11-2 plants, respectively.
source: Re-introduction of a UBP22 or SGF11 functional coding sequence successfully restored low H2Bub levels in ubp22-1 and sgf11-2 plants, respectively (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by complementation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Comparison with the ubp26-4 mutant line showed a more pronounced effect in ubp22-1.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, comparison with the previously identified histone H2Bub deubiquitination mutant line ubp26-4 (Schmitz et al., 2009), showed a pronounced effect in ubp22-1.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: UBP22 constitutes a major determinant of histone H2Bub deubiquitination and is necessary to maintain normal levels of H2Bub in Arabidopsis.
source: These observations indicate that UBP22 constitutes a major determinant of histone H2Bub deubiquitination and is necessary to maintain normal levels of H2Bub in Arabidopsis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic and biochemical data presented.

claim: Analysis of GFP-SGF11 expressed under the control of a 35S promoter showed lower levels in protein extracts from dark-grown than in light-grown seedlings.
source: Considering the dual effects of light and of DET1 loss-of-function on H2Bub levels on one hand, and the physical association of DDA1 with the DUBm component SGF11 on the other, we tested whether SGF11 protein abundance was influenced by light conditions. Analysis of GFP-SGF11 expressed under the control of a 35S promoter (35S::GFP-SGF11 plants) indeed showed lower levels in protein extracts from dark-grown than in light-grown seedlings (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Pre-incubation of the plants with the MG132 proteasome inhibitor largely increased GFP-SGF11 accumulation to similar levels in both light and dark conditions.
source: Pre-incubation of the plants with the MG132 proteasome inhibitor largely increased GFP-SGF11 accumulation to similar levels in both conditions.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Similar effects of MG132 treatment were observed for the ENY2 and UBP22 proteins.
source: Similar effects were observed for the ENY2 and UBP22 proteins (Figure 6A), showing that abundance of all DUBm subunits is tightly controlled.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Abundance of all DUBm subunits is tightly controlled.
source: Similar effects were observed for the ENY2 and UBP22 proteins (Figure 6A), showing that abundance of all DUBm subunits is tightly controlled.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the MG132 treatment data.

claim: SGF11 proteins are poly-ubiquitinated under both dark and light conditions, with a more pronounced effect in darkness.
source: Affinity purification of protein extracts from 35S::MYC-SGF11 seedlings with a ubiquitin-affinity resin showed that SGF11 proteins are poly-ubiquitinated under both dark and light conditions, with a more pronounced effect in darkness (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitin pull-down data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Stability of SGF11 is controlled by a proteasomal activity with a more prevalent effect in darkness.
source: We concluded that stability of SGF11 is controlled by a proteasomal activity with a more prevalent effect in darkness.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the MG132 and ubiquitin pull-down data.

claim: DET1 is required for SGF11 and UBP22 proteolytic degradation.
source: Given the established role of the C3D complex in promoting protein degradation in darkness, we further tested whether the effect of light on SGF11 stability is mediated by DET1 after introgression of the det1-1 allele in the 35S::MYC-SGF11 and 35S::GFP-UBP22 transgenic lines. Levels of both MYC-SGF11 and GFP-UBP22 were higher in det1-1 than in wild-type plants in both conditions, indicating that DET1 is indeed required for SGF11 and UBP22 proteolytic degradation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Steady-state levels of the constitutively expressed recombinant MYC-SGF11 and GFP-UBP22 proteins exhibited dramatic changes during light-to-dark and dark-to-light transitions.
source: To test for a dynamic regulation of SGF11 and UBP22 stability by light signaling, the 35S::MYC-SGF11 and 35S::GFP-UBP22 transgenic lines were submitted to dark-to-light and light-to-dark switches. Steady-state levels of the constitutively expressed recombinant MYC-SGF11 and GFP-UBP22 proteins exhibited dramatic changes during the transitions, which were already visible after 24 hr upon the transitions (Figure 6D, top panels).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Changes in MYC-SGF11 and GFP-UBP22 levels during light transitions were robustly dampened in the det1-1 genetic background.
source: Furthermore, these changes were robustly dampened in the det1-1 genetic background (Figure 6D, bottom panels).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Stability of the DUBm complex is regulated by the light signaling factor DET1.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that stability of the DUBm complex is regulated by the light signaling factor DET1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the protein stability data presented.

claim: Immunoblot analyses showed increased H2Bub levels in det1-1ubp22-1 as compared to det1-1 single mutant seedlings.
source: Our findings point towards a model in which DET1 influences H2Bub homeostasis by opposing DUBm activity. To examine this possible antagonistic influence, we crossed the det1-1 and ubp22-1 lines and probed global H2Bub levels in double mutant plants. Immunoblot analyses indeed showed increased H2Bub levels in det1-1ubp22-1 as compared to det1-1 single mutant seedlings.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Loss of H2Bub triggered by det1-1 is partially suppressed in the absence of a functional DUBm.
source: Hence, loss of H2Bub triggered by det1-1 is partially suppressed in the absence of a functional DUBm (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The ubp22-1 mutation partially suppressed the constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype of det1-1 seedlings.
source: To provide a more functional assessment on the antagonistic activities of DET1 and DUBm, we determined the photomorphogenic phenotype of ubp22-1 and det1-1ubp22-1 seedlings by measuring hypocotyl length upon growth in darkness. Again, the ubp22-1 mutation partially suppressed the constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype of det1-1 seedlings (Chory et al., 1989), whereas UBP22 overexpression on its own did not affect hypocotyl elongation (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by hypocotyl measurement data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: UBP22 overexpression on its own did not affect hypocotyl elongation.
source: Again, the ubp22-1 mutation partially suppressed the constitutive photomorphogenic phenotype of det1-1 seedlings (Chory et al., 1989), whereas UBP22 overexpression on its own did not affect hypocotyl elongation (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by hypocotyl measurement data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: UBP22 loss-of-function only marginally affects transcript levels - with just 26 genes being misregulated in ubp22-1 as compared to WT plants.
source: Secondly, we determined the transcriptome profile of det1-1ubp22-1 seedlings and compared it with those of WT, det1-1 and ubp22-1 plants. As reported for the yeast ubp8∆ strain (Gardner et al., 2005; Lenstra et al., 2011), differential analyses of gene expression showed that UBP22 loss-of-function only marginally affects transcript levels - with just 26 genes being misregulated in ubp22-1 as compared to WT plants (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7C and citations to yeast studies.

claim: det1-1ubp22-1 double mutant plants displayed a partially suppressed transcriptome profile as compared to det1-1 plants, the expression of about half (53%) of the genes misregulated in det1-1 seedlings being restored by UBP22 loss-of-function.
source: In line with the hypothesis of C3D opposing DUBm activity, det1-1ubp22-1 double mutant plants displayed a partially suppressed transcriptome profile as compared to det1-1 plants, the expression of about half (53%) of the genes misregulated in det1-1 seedlings being restored by UBP22 loss-of-function (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Independent transgenic lines in which UBP22-GFP is overexpressed confirm that UBP22 is a limiting factor in H2Bub removal.
source: Our conclusions on C3D function therefore predict that over-accumulation of the DUBm in det1-1 plants is responsible, at least partially, for the reduction of H2Bub levels in det1-1 plants. Independent transgenic lines in which UBP22-GFP is overexpressed (wt/UBP22-GFP#OE1 and #OE2) indeed confirm that UBP22 is a limiting factor in H2Bub removal (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7D (likely a typo in the text, should be 7D not 7E).

claim: DET1-mediated control of DUBm proteolytic degradation represents a previously unidentified mechanism to adjust H2Bub levels, which can mediate light-dependent control on H2Bub homeostasis over the genome.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that DET1-mediated control of DUBm proteolytic degradation represents a previously unidentified mechanism to adjust H2Bub levels, which can mediate light-dependent control on H2Bub homeostasis over the genome.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all the data presented.
